6.1.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "a painful loose hip — what do you think first?"
- "A loose implant is **septic until proved otherwise** → infection work-up before any revision."
- "**Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI)** hits ≈1% of hips; implant **biofilm** decides keep or exchange."
- "Classify by **time** → early and stable: **keep** the implant · late or loose: **exchange** it."

### Loosening — septic or aseptic?
- **Loosening** = failed fixation, never achieved or lost later, with no active mechanical cause
- Counts → previous dislocation, healed fracture · does not → **acute fracture**, **active dislocation**
- First split → **septic** vs **aseptic** → treatment differs completely
- Clinical picture of aseptic loosening → 7 Loosening

CLINICAL PEARL — beware septic loosening
- Exclude **septic loosening** even when the case looks aseptic (Prof Sherif Khaled)
- Loose in the **first few years** → think infection or failed fixation, not wear

### Incidence & why biofilm matters
- Incidence → ≈**1%** hip and shoulder, ≈**2%** knee (Handbook)
- Infection leads **early** revisions · aseptic loosening dominates **later** ones
- Draining wound → **no oral antibiotics before cultures** → they mask the organism

#### Biofilm — why a late implant must come out
- **Biofilm** = bacteria in a matrix on the implant → shielded from antibiotics and phagocytes → reservoir
- **1000–10,000×** more resistant · covers a surface in **4–8 days** (Miller)
[[FIG: Fig 6.1 · 6.1
- Mature biofilm cannot be cleaned in place → implant out + all dead tissue out

### Organisms & routes
| Organism | Share of PJI (Campbell) | Picture |
|---|---|---|
| **S. aureus** | 29–40% | aggressive → hot acute joint |
| **CoNS** (coagulase-negative staph), e.g. S. epidermidis | 13–36% | low virulence, biofilm → quiet chronic pain |
| Streptococci, enterococci, gram-negatives | minority | haematogenous · resistant, with a sinus |

- Routes → **inoculation at surgery** (most) · local wound spread · **haematogenous** · reactivated old septic hip
- Late haematogenous sources → **dental**, **urinary**, **skin**
- Case → infected Thompson, **Enterobacter** sensitive only to colistin and tigecycline → renal risk → **colistin**

### Risk factors
| General → weak immunity, healing | Local → poor soft-tissue envelope |
|---|---|
| Age · **diabetes** · renal or liver disease | Vascular compromise · venous congestion · prior DVT (deep vein thrombosis) |
| Malnutrition · **smoking** · **obesity** · alcohol | Neuropathy · prior radiation · local trauma |
| Immunosuppression · inflammatory arthritis, e.g. RA (rheumatoid arthritis) | Prior surgery on this hip · previous joint infection |

- Non-modifiable, worse outcome → inflammatory arthritis, immunosuppression, diabetes, prior surgery or infection
- Before elective THA (total hip arthroplasty) → optimise **glucose**, stop **smoking**, weight, **nutrition**

### Classification — Tsukayama & Trampuz
- Every timing scheme asks → **is the biofilm mature yet?** → keep or exchange

| Tsukayama, not "Sugiyama" (Campbell) | Definition |
|---|---|
| 1 · **Early postoperative** | onset in the first **month** |
| 2 · **Late chronic** | >1 month, **insidious** → seeded at surgery, slow organism |
| 3 · **Acute haematogenous** | >1 month, **acute**, well-working hip, distant source |
| 4 · **Positive intraoperative cultures** | at revision for "aseptic" loosening |

| Trampuz–Zimmerli | Prosthesis | Internal fixation | Usual origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Early** | <3 months | <2 weeks | surgery, high virulence |
| **Delayed** | 3–24 months | 2–10 weeks | surgery, low virulence |
| **Late** | >24 months | >10 weeks | haematogenous |

- Positive intraoperative cultures → targeted antibiotics · **McPherson** → adds host and limb grades → predicts outcome

#### Acute vs chronic — the split that drives treatment
- **Acute** → <4 weeks after surgery · or an old hip with sudden symptoms <3 weeks = **acute haematogenous**
- **Chronic** → >4 weeks, or haematogenous symptoms for 2–3 months → **revision** (Prof Abdel Moneim)

PITFALL — where does "acute" end?
- Course and Tsukayama → **4 weeks** after surgery · Miller → **<3 weeks** of symptoms · Trampuz → **3 months**
- Say → "**about 4 weeks after surgery, or under 3 weeks of symptoms** → biofilm young → keep the implant"

6.2.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you diagnose PJI?"
- "History, then **ESR and CRP** (erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein) → raised or suspicious → **aspirate** off antibiotics."
- "Fluid → cell count, **PMN %** (polymorphonuclear neutrophils), culture → scored by **ICM 2018** (International Consensus Meeting)."
- "**1 major** or **≥6 points** = infected · at surgery → **5 samples**, frozen section, sonication."

### Clinical picture
- Acute → **fever**, malaise, **rest pain**, hot swollen joint ± collection or **sinus**
- Chronic → often **pain only**, quiet wound → no systemic signs ≠ no infection

#### History that raises suspicion
- **Pain never settled** · prolonged wound drainage · repeated antibiotics · discharge or prior infection
- Rule → **every patient infected until proved otherwise** (Prof Abdel Karim)
- Case → 30 years, **AVN** (avascular necrosis) → THA · at 3 weeks hot, tender, painful, serous discharge
[[FIG: Fig 6.3 · 6.2

### Imaging
- **Septic loosening** → periostitis, reactive bone, **endosteal scalloping**, lucent zones growing week by week
- **Normal X-ray ≠ no infection** → insensitive early, mimics aseptic loosening
- **Sinogram** → dye reaching the prosthesis confirms PJI · **CT, MRI** → do not confirm infection

| Scan | Shows | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Technetium-99m** bone scan | bone turnover | false positive **1–2 years**, cementless longer · negative reassures (Prof Abdel Karim) |
| **Indium-111** white cells | infection | both positive = septic · technetium alone = aseptic |
| + **Sulfur colloid** marrow | normal marrow | separates marrow from infection |

- Scans only when other tests leave doubt
[[FIG: Fig 6.4 · 6.2

### Blood tests
- Leukocytosis, positive blood cultures → acute sepsis · normal **WBC** (white blood cells) common in chronic PJI
- **ESR + CRP** = universal screen · both normal → ≈5% still infected: negative predictive value **95%** (Prof Abdel Karim)
- ESR fading · **CRP** more specific → abnormal, or low-virulence doubt (Cutibacterium, CoNS) → **aspirate**
[[FIG: Fig 6.5 · 6.2
- After any surgery → CRP settles in **weeks**, ESR in **months**

### Aspiration — getting it right
| Rule (Prof Abdel Karim) | Why |
|---|---|
| Off antibiotics **14 days** | false-negative cultures |
| **Extended culture**, 9–14 days | slow organisms, e.g. CoNS |
| **Blood-culture bottles** → yield up to 9× | an ordinary pot loses organisms |
| **Total + differential count with PMN** + culture | common error: culture only |
| **Dry tap** → never inject saline | brings infection in |

- Technique → sterile prep, **18-gauge spinal needle**, fluoroscopy or ultrasound, until it touches the metal neck
[[FIG: Fig 6.6 · 6.2
- No sinus, no prior cultures → **aspirate first** → organism and antibiotic unknown
[[FIG: Fig 6.7 · 6.2
- **Sinus** → no aspiration → culture the sinus · ESR/CRP = follow-up baseline only
- Histology → **CT-guided biopsy** confirms

### ICM 2018 criteria — one score
- Path → **MSIS** (Musculoskeletal Infection Society) → **ICM** Philadelphia 2013 → ICM 2018 score
- 2013 minor → **3 of 5**: CRP + ESR, synovial WBC, LE, PMN %, histology
- 2018 → same major criteria · minor criteria → **weighted score**
[[FIG: Fig 6.8 · 6.2

| ICM 2018 (Campbell) | Acute | Chronic | Points |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Major** → 2 cultures, same organism · **or** sinus to the prosthesis | — | — | = **infected** |
| Serum **CRP** (mg/L) **or** **D-dimer** (ng/mL) | >100 · unknown | >10 · >860 | **2** |
| Serum **ESR** (mm/h) | no role | >30 | **1** |
| Synovial **WBC** **or** **LE** (leukocyte esterase) **or** **alpha-defensin** | >10,000 · 2+ · ≥1.0 | >3,000 · 2+ · ≥1.0 | **3** |
| Synovial **PMN** % | >90 | >70 | **2** |
| **Single** positive culture | — | — | **2** |
| Positive **histology** (frozen section) | — | — | **3** |
| Intraoperative **purulence** (not with ALTR, adverse local tissue reaction) | — | — | **3** |
| **Combined pre- + intraoperative score** | | | **≥6 infected · 3–5 inconclusive → molecular tests · <3 not infected** |

- "**Or**" rows score **once** · synovial tests weigh most → they sample the joint
- Acute thresholds much higher → the operation itself inflames the joint
- Caution → **ALTR** and slow organisms · tests on offer: serum, synovial, imaging, tissue
[[FIG: Fig 6.9 · 6.2

PITFALL — D-dimer threshold: 850 or 860?
- Course and Campbell text → **850 ng/mL** · ICM table → **>860** · later work → **fibrinogen** better
- Say → "**D-dimer above ≈850 (860 in the ICM table) scores 2 points, instead of CRP**"

### Synovial tests — and their traps
- **LE** → urine strip turns **pink**: activated-neutrophil enzyme · read **2+** → sensitivity 80–100% (Prof Abdel Karim)
- **Blood** in the sample → false reading · keep strips **in theatre**
- **Alpha-defensin** → **unaffected by antibiotics** · **ALTR → false positive**
[[FIG: Fig 6.10 · 6.2
- **Synovial CRP** + alpha-defensin → settles equivocal results

### At surgery — samples & newer methods
- **3–5 samples**, best **5**, odd number → capsule, acetabulum, femur (Prof Abdel Karim)
- Odd → one may be contaminated → 3 of 5 positive beats 1–2
- Sample **every revision** → tissue may grow other organisms: polymicrobial, low virulence

| Method | What it adds |
|---|---|
| **Frozen section** | **≥5 neutrophils per HPF** (high-power field) in 5 fields (Miller) · expert pathologist, 15–20 min |
| **Sonication** of the implant | breaks biofilm → better yield, esp. culture-negative |
| **NGS** (next-generation sequencing) | positive ≈90% vs culture 61% (Prof Abdel Karim) |
| **ICM Philly app** | data → score → next step |
[[FIG: Fig 6.11 · 6.2

### Culture-negative PJI
- Culture-negative **5–42%** → repeat off antibiotics 14 days, or **PCR** (polymerase chain reaction) (Prof Abdel Karim)
- Negative culture ≠ no infection · **Gram stain** and systemic WBC → not supported
- **Multifactorial** diagnosis → no single test: not Synovasure, ESR or CRP alone

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **ESR/CRP → aspirate off antibiotics → 3,000 / 70% / 2+ → 1 major or 6 points → 5 samples**

6.3.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you treat an infected THA?"
- "Decide by **time**, **implant stability**, **organism**, **host** → early + stable: **DAIR** (debridement, antibiotics, implant retention)."
- "Chronic or loose → **two-stage exchange**, the gold standard → all out, **antibiotic spacer**, reimplant later."
- "**One-stage** → fit host, known sensitive organism, no sinus · unfit → **suppression** or **resection**."

### Prevention
| Phase | Measures |
|---|---|
| **Before** | treat septic foci · short stay · stop smoking **6 months** before and after (Prof Ihab Desouky) · decolonise **S. aureus**: nasal mupirocin, chlorhexidine |
| **Skin** | no nail polish, no lotions · antibacterial soap shower · hair → **clip only if needed, just before surgery; never a razor, never the night before** (Campbell) |
| **Theatre** | **HEPA** (high-efficiency particulate air) filters · **laminar flow** · UV light · minimal traffic |
| **Technique** | full PPE (personal protective equipment) · gentle tissues · haemostasis · **antibiotic-loaded cement** |
| **Drains** | optional → out by **48 h**, or 24 h if <50 mL (Handbook) |

#### Antibiotic prophylaxis — the most important single measure
| Drug | Dose (Campbell) | When |
|---|---|---|
| **Cefazolin** (or cefuroxime) | 2 g, redose every 4 h | first choice |
| **Vancomycin** | 15–20 mg/kg | resistant S. aureus carrier |
| **Clindamycin** | 600–900 mg | cephalosporin allergy |

- Timing → within **1 h** before anaesthesia, ≥15 min before the tourniquet · stop by **24 h** (Handbook; Miller)
- **Any revision** → rule out infection, always culture, spacer on standby

### Management — choose by four questions
- Start with **classification** → acute vs chronic, tailored per case
- **Time** → <4 weeks: young biofilm, clearable · >4 weeks: mature → exchange
- **Loose implant → always exchange**, at any duration → its interface cannot be cleaned

| Option | Use it when | Key point |
|---|---|---|
| **DAIR** | <4 weeks or acute haematogenous · **stable** implant | swap head and liner |
| **One-stage** | fit host · known sensitive low-virulence organism · no sinus | selected cases |
| **Two-stage** | chronic · loose · resistant or unknown organism · sinus · failed DAIR | gold standard |
| **Suppression** | unfit for or refusing surgery | controls, does not cure |
| **Resection** | non-ambulant · repeated failure · no bone or soft tissue | infection control high, function poor |

### Suppressive antibiotics
- Single indication → **unfit** patient · stopped → infection **flares**
- **Rifampicin** + a partner for staphylococci on a retained implant → acts on biofilm · never alone → resistance

PITFALL — how long is suppression?
- Handbook → **6-month** course, 20–60% success · Campbell → **lifelong**, ≈67% success
- Say → "**unfit only, usually for life → stopping lets 80% flare** (Prof Abdel Moneim)"

### DAIR — Debridement, Antibiotics & Implant Retention
- Indication → **<4 weeks**, **stable** implant · superficial (skin, fat) or deep (fascia → joint) debridement

#### Steps
- Dislocate, **remove head and liner**, debride layer by layer, 5 cultures, irrigate, fresh drapes, **new head and liner**
- **Modular exchange** → reaches behind the liner · none → ≈**4×** failure · survival **52% → 79%** (Prof Abdel Moneim)
- **Bulb syringe**, not **pulsatile lavage** → high pressure drives organisms deeper, seeds new areas
[[FIG: Fig 6.12 · 6.3

#### Results
- Needs good immunity, good general condition, **early** surgery
- Success ≈**65–70%** · high-risk host **16–28%** (Prof Abdel Moneim)

CLINICAL PEARL — time is the implant
- Key success factor → **interval from index operation to DAIR**
- Case at 3 weeks → **do not wait** · a delay of 5–9 days → chronic
- After DAIR → IV (intravenous) antibiotics **4–6 weeks** · failed → **no second DAIR** → exchange (Miller)

### Two-stage exchange — the gold standard
- Indications → >4 weeks **or** loose · immunocompromised · previous failures · failed DAIR
- Price → two operations, months of poor function · repeats → morbidity, cost, **arthrofibrosis**
- **Three-stage** → resistant virulent organism, severe infection → re-debride at **2–4 weeks**

#### Stage 1 — out with everything
- **All implants + all cement** out, debride, antibiotic spacer · **VAC** (vacuum dressing) contraindicated
- Cement → reamed gradually with **tibial nail reamers**, or out via a **femoral osteotomy** → bone preserved
[[FIG: Fig 6.13 · 6.3

#### Antibiotic cement
| Rule (Prof Abdel Moneim) | Reason |
|---|---|
| **Hand mixing**, not vacuum | more pores → more elution |
| **Heat-stable**, **water-soluble** powder | survives polymerisation, elutes |
| **Two drugs**, not gentamicin alone | synergism |

- Dose per 40 g of PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate) → 2 Fixation
[[FIG: Fig 6.14 · 6.3

#### Spacers
| | **Static** | **Articulating** |
|---|---|---|
| What | cement block in the acetabulum ± cement rod | PROSTALAC (prosthesis of antibiotic-loaded acrylic cement), ready-made, or moulded on a **Steinmann pin** |
| Pros | big bone loss, lost stability | motion, no contracture, leg length, easier reimplantation |
| Cons | stiffness, contracture, harder second stage | dislocation, spacer fracture |
[[FIG: Fig 6.15 · 6.3

- **PROSTALAC** → a simple total hip the patient moves on · static → when the acetabulum cannot hold one
[[FIG: Fig 6.16 · 6.3

#### Spacer rules (Prof Abdel Moneim)
- **Extra-small stem** → most cement, most elution · put in **loose** → easy removal
- PROSTALAC → less dislocation than a G-stem, less erosion than a hemi spacer
- G-stem elutes only **4–6 weeks** → then a foreign body → biofilm

#### Interval & stage 2
- **IV 2 weeks → oral 4 weeks** · **no drug holiday** → resistance, reinfection (Prof Abdel Moneim)
- Spacer **2–3 months** → longer → loosening, periprosthetic fracture
- Campbell's school → reimplant at ≈**3 months** if ESR/CRP fall and an aspirate 2 weeks off antibiotics is clean

#### Stage 2 — reimplantation
- Needs → resolved signs, **normal CRP**, negative aspirate, blood cultures, intraoperative biopsy (Handbook)
- Normal CRP ≠ eradication → hence Campbell's repeat aspiration

#### Reconstruction
- **CT** plan → cavitary vs segmental defects · revision implants ready
[[FIG: Fig 6.17 · 6.3
- **Reinforcement ring** → cup **cemented**, never press-fit: no metal on metal
[[FIG: Fig 6.18 · 6.3
- Example → osteotomy, spacer, healed osteotomy, new stem
[[FIG: Fig 6.19 · 6.3

### One-stage exchange
